Fit a Flexible Residual Point Process

ffit.Rd

Estimate a composition model using an FRPP likelihood. Reuses the public emhawkes parameter map and optimizer adapters and restores an fspec.

Usage

ffit(object, inter_arrival, type = NULL, mark = NULL,
     N = NULL, Nc = NULL, N0 = NULL, Nc0 = NULL,
     lambda_component0 = "auto", estimate_residual = FALSE,
     optimizer = c("maxLik", "stats"), method = "BFGS",
     backend = c("bridge", "state"), reduced = TRUE,
     fixed = NULL, constraints = NULL, constraint = NULL,
     valid = NULL, ...)
fitted_fspec(object)
finitial_state(object)
fdiagnostics(object)

Arguments

object

An fspec for fitting, or an ffit result for the helpers.

inter_arrival, type, mark

Observed intervals, event types and optional marks, including an initial zero row.

N, Nc

Optional cumulative count and mark-total paths.

N0, Nc0

Initial counts and mark totals.

lambda_component0

Initial kernel components. "auto" selects zero; specify a scalar or conformable matrix when known. Hawkes mean initialization is not used.

estimate_residual

Keep the residual distribution fixed by default. Set TRUE to include its named parameters in the optimization.

optimizer

Optional maxLik provider, or R's stats provider through the public emhawkes adapter. The stats provider does not require maxLik.

method

Optimization method, default BFGS. The stats provider also supports Nelder-Mead, CG and L-BFGS-B.

backend

FRPP likelihood backend. state retains the numeric-kernel restrictions described in logLik.fspec.

reduced

Share entries having equal starting values within each numeric kernel matrix. Function parameters sharing a name are shared under either setting.

fixed

Logical mask or parameter positions, passed to the optimizer. With stats, names are also supported. The order follows emhawkes: mu, alpha, beta, eta, impact, mark density, residual density/CDF/quantile; duplicated function parameter names occur once. Fixed residual parameters are excluded entirely when estimate_residual = FALSE.

constraints, constraint

Alternative names for optimization constraints. Supply at most one. Linear inequalities are list(ineqA, ineqB) with \(A\theta+B\ge0\); columns follow the full parameter order, including fixed optimization parameters. Stats uses constrOptim and requires a strictly interior start for movable inequalities; it does not support equalities.

valid

Optional function of the named full parameter vector, returning one nonmissing logical value. FALSE rejects a proposal with minus infinity. Fixed raw residual parameters are also included. Validator and callback errors propagate. Supply distribution-specific domain checks when needed.

...

Named optimizer arguments accepted by the public hfit adapter, including control, grad, hess, and stats box bounds. For stats use control$maxit; maxLik uses control$iterlim. FRPP objective, analytic Hawkes gradient and Hawkes final-Hessian selection cannot be overridden through these arguments.

Details

The new fitting API delegates parameter sharing, optimization and kernel reconstruction to public emhawkes functions; its objective always evaluates the FRPP model. No internal emhawkes functions or Hawkes curvature stabilization are used. Likelihood evaluation and default BFGS fitting do not generate random values. Stochastic optimizers can consume randomness. User callbacks must be deterministic.

Residual parameters are fixed by default to avoid silently estimating two confounded scales. Joint estimation requires an identifiable model: fixing or normalizing the relevant scale remains the user's modeling choice. This API does not automatically diagnose all forms of nonidentification or normalize arbitrary laws. Matrix sharing is preserved on reconstruction; residual parameters shared among density, CDF, quantile and generator functions are updated together.

The result supports coef, logLik, nobs, vcov, summary and fitted. fitted_fspec and fitted return the estimated composition model; finitial_state returns the initialization arguments for likelihood replay or simulation. Save the result with saveRDS and restore it with readRDS. Captured callback environments remain references; external state is not frozen.

Wald covariance is withheld on optimizer failure, missing or nonpositive curvature, near detected constraint boundaries, and equality constraints. The original provider result remains in fit$fit. A positive covariance is reported as available_unvalidated: numerical step sensitivity, nonsmooth densities, weak identification and actual confidence-interval coverage have not been validated. A supplied analytic Hessian can avoid finite-difference error for a smooth model. No eigenvalue clipping or absolute-variance correction is used. The tzexp transition may give a nonsmooth optimum; consider profile likelihood or bootstrap separately rather than interpreting a success code as valid inference.

Value

ffit returns a list of class ffit, including the provider fit, estimated fspec, coefficients, covariance, likelihood, initialization and diagnostics. fitted_fspec returns an fspec, finitial_state a list, and fdiagnostics a list containing convergence and Wald-availability information. Likelihood degrees of freedom count only active optimization parameters; nobs excludes the initial row. Unavailable free-parameter covariance entries are NA.

Examples

model <- fspec(methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1),
  residual_law(c(rate = 1), stats::dexp, stats::pexp, stats::qexp, stats::rexp))
fit <- ffit(model, c(0, .2, .3, .5), optimizer = "stats",
  fixed = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), lambda_component0 = 0)
coef(fit)
#>    mu1 alpha1  beta1 
#>      3      0      1 
summary(fit)
#> FRPP maximum likelihood fit (stats, BFGS, bridge)
#> Log likelihood: 0.2958369
#> Convergence code: 0 (Normal convergence.)
#>        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> mu1      3.0000     1.7321  1.7321  0.08326 .
#> alpha1   0.0000     0.0000      NA       NA  
#> beta1    1.0000     0.0000      NA       NA  
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> Fixed parameters: alpha1, beta1
#> Wald covariance: available_unvalidated
fdiagnostics(fit)
#> $optimizer
#> [1] "stats"
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "BFGS"
#> 
#> $backend
#> [1] "bridge"
#> 
#> $optimizer_code
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $optimizer_message
#> [1] "Normal convergence."
#> 
#> $optimizer_success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $estimate_residual
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $wald
#> [1] "available_unvalidated"
#> 
#> $reason
#> NULL
#> 
#> $active
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
#> 
#> $note
#> [1] "Optimizer curvature is not a validation of FRPP Wald coverage; no Hawkes Hessian stabilization is applied."
#> 
estimated <- fitted(fit)
do.call(logLik, c(list(object = estimated, inter_arrival = c(0, .2, .3, .5)),
  finitial_state(fit)))
#> loglikelihood 
#>     0.2958369
